comments.story_title: Why Wolfram Tech Isn’t Open Source
comments.why_zh: Blender 如何成为开源软件，而不是沦为弃置软件。
comments.quote_zh: 我强烈建议大家把整篇采访看完
comments.text_zh: 你最后那句话让我想起了对 Blender 创始人 Ton Rosendaal 的一篇采访。他详细谈到了 Blender 是如何变成开源软件、而不是沦为弃置软件的。我强烈建议大家把整篇采访看完（你至少需要 5 分钟才能习惯他的口音），但关键部分大约从第 14 分钟开始 [VIDEO]
comments.text: Your last sentence reminded me of an interview with the Ton Rosendaal, the creator of Blender. He talks extensively about how Blender became OSS and not abandonware. I highly encourage to watch the whole interview (you need at least 5 mins to get used to his accent), but the important part starts around minute 14 [VIDEO]

comments.author: greshario
comments.why_zh: Ton Roosendaal说钱只是用于创作的工具。
comments.quote_zh: 我推荐看看他的这场访谈
comments.text_zh: 我推荐看看他的这场访谈——至少看看他谈到钱的部分。听到一位在科技领域处于顶尖水平的人说，除了作为帮助自己创作的工具之外，他对钱不感兴趣，这让人感到无比耳目一新。[VIDEO]
comments.text: I reccomend watching this interview with him - at least the parts where he talks about money. It's incredibly refreshing to hear someone at the top of their game in the tech sphere say they're not interested in money except as a tool to help them create. [VIDEO]

comments.author: solarkraft
comments.why_zh: Blender以对创作者可用性为重点的迭代开发。
comments.text_zh: Blender的故事是一个相当令人印象深刻的迭代开发故事。Ton Rosensaal非常明确地不想要为技术而技术，而是想要“把它发布出去”，但同时始终关注它对创作者是否好用（现在比过去更是如此，但基础早就打好了，看看所有东西都可动画化这一点）。和Blender Guru的精彩访谈：[VIDEO]
comments.text: The Blender story is quite an impressive one of iterative development. Ton Rosensaal very explicitly doesn't want technology for its own sake and wants to "get it out of the door", but does it all while keeping an eye on it being usable for creatives (now more than before, but the ground work was laid long ago, see everything being animatable) Great interview with Blender Guru: [VIDEO]

comments.author: solarkraft
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What was the best software that you used during 2022?

comments.text_zh: 如果我没记错的话，Blender 的创造者 Ton Rosendaal 仍在领导这个项目，但他非常仔细地倾听用户及其痛点，并且采用了一种非常有趣的软件开发方式。和 BlenderGuru 的那次采访非常棒：[VIDEO] 上一次重大重新设计，源于采访者分享的一个愿景，而他似乎正是众多深度投入的艺术家之一。（这全都非常“如果我没记错的话”，基于我多年前间接听到或看到的东西）
comments.text: IIRC Ton Rosendaal, Blender's creator, still leads the project, but while listening very closely to its users and their pains and a very interesting approach to software development. The interview with BlenderGuru is great one: [VIDEO] The last major redesign was started by a vision shared by the interviewer, who seems to be one of the many deeply invested artists. (This is all very much "IIRC", based on stuff I've peripherally heard or seen years ago)

comments.author: invader
comments.story_title: Ton Roosendaal to step down as Blender chairman and CEO
comments.why_zh: Ton Roosendaal 回顾了 Blender 从 Amiga 到众筹的历程。
comments.text_zh: Ton 是个传奇，也是我个人的英雄。他是一位伟大的创新者，也是一位开源巨星，颠覆了整个传统上由大公司主导的行业。整个 Blender 的故事都很吸引人——从 Amiga 上的建模器和光线追踪器原型，到互联网泡沫时期的创业公司，再到那场著名的让 Blender 自由的众筹活动……这是一个值得拍成电影的故事。对于任何对开源历史感兴趣、但不熟悉 Blender 故事的人，我都会强烈推荐 Ton 接受 Blender Guru 的那次采访，他在其中回顾了自己的历程——[VIDEO]
comments.text: Ton is a legend and a personal hero of mine. He is a great innovator and an open-source superstar who disrupted the entire industry, traditionally dominated by big corporations. The entire Blender story is captivating - from modeler and raytracer prototypes on Amiga to the Internet bubble startup to the famous crowdfunding campaign to free Blender... It is a story that deserves a movie. For anyone interested in open-source history who is not familiar with the Blender story, I would highly recommend Ton's interview with Blender Guru, where he reflects on his journey - [VIDEO]

comments.author: Lievelingsduif
comments.why_zh: Blender的历史，包括通过众筹转向开源。
comments.quote_zh: Ton Roosendaal和Blender Guru之间关于这段历史的有趣访谈
comments.text_zh: 在2.7 UI更新之前，Blender就已经拥有稳固且热情的用户群体。Blender也是率先采用类似Kickstarter的方案来筹集足够资金将其开源的。Ton Roosendaal和Blender Guru之间有一场关于这段历史的有趣访谈。[VIDEO] Blender团队对那些试图改进UX等东西的人也没那么敌视。GIMP也迫切需要做的一件事就是改名；Blender这个名字虽然古怪，但至少不会让人联想到色情图像。
comments.text: Blender already has a solid and enthousiastic user base before the 2.7 UI update. Blender was also the forerunner in having a kickstarter-like scheme to raise enough money to make it opensource. There's an interesting interview between Ton Roosendaal and Blender Guru about the history. [VIDEO] The Blender guys were also a lot less hostile towards people trying to make improvements to stuff like UX. One of the things that GIMP also desperately needs is a name change, while Blender is an odd choice it at least doesn't conjur up sexual images.

comments.text: Ton Roosendaal (Blender creator) estimated in 2018 interview that 3D software market is very small, and pulled up Autodesk's (3DsMax/Maya, etc) business results from that time, which amounted to 25000 - 30000 yearly licenses. He also claimed that Maya has "maybe 20" developers behind with things being similar for other products. [VIDEO] (jump to 1h mark)

comments.story_title: Don't End the Week with Nothing (2014)
comments.text_zh: > 那我来问一下……你听播客的时候，有没有从中得到过任何可付诸行动的东西？你会做笔记吗？你会总结吗？我可以从自己的角度稍微回答一下。我个人使用的科技播客有三大灵感来源。前两个：[LINK] 和 [LINK]，都是“老手互相聊各自的职业生涯和学到的东西”的形式。它们总是以两个老朋友叙旧的方式展开，但会沿着他们的人生、经历和一路上的学习收获有引导地聊。这些就是我想效仿的，不过会聚焦于面向企业、商业和初创公司的编程。我个人最兴奋的是和那些我非常尊敬地称为“cogwheel”或“workhorse”的开发者交谈。我觉得与其他创作者相比，开发者得到的赞誉远远不够……比如某个能按需哭出来的人能拿到一座小金像和掌声……但那个把1500行SQL重写成一行、把一周的工作缩短到几秒钟的人却没有？！你是说我还得自己出去买一座属于我的小金像，再在手机上循环播放掌声？这太扯了！至少这是我想开始的地方。过去几天我看了一些采访，比如Blender的创造者Ton Roosendaal的[VIDEO]。等我培养出采访技巧，能去和那些真正让我觉得自己有点像编程迷弟的人交谈之后……
comments.text: > So let me ask ... when you're listening to podcasts, do you ever take anything away from them that is actionable? Do you take notes? Do you summarise? I can answer this a little from my perspective. There are three major inspirations for tech podcasts that I use personally. The first two: [LINK] and [LINK] are both in the format of "veterans talk to each other about their careers and the things they've learned". They always roll in the format of two old friends catching up, but in a guided way in terms of their life, experiences and learnings from along the way. These are the ones that I want to emulate, but with a focus on programming for enterprise, business and startups. I'm personally most excited in talking to what I think of very respectfully as "cogwheel" or "workhorse" developers. I think developers are vastly under-celebrated when compared to other creatives ... like some person who can cry on demand gets a tiny golden statue and applause ... but the person who re-writes 1500 lines of SQL into a one liner and reduces a week long job down to seconds DOESN'T?! You're telling me I have to go out and buy my OWN tiny little golden statue and play an applause loop on my cellphone? That's bullshit! At least that's where I want to start, I've seen some interviews in the last few days with people like Ton Roosendaal - the creator of blender - [VIDEO] After I've developed the interview skills to talk to the people who genuinely make me feel a little like a programming fanboy
